title: onprem: airgap offline bundle - vendor rke2 arm64 support + TUF updates
author: Priya Nambiar
release_notes: Adds arm64 vendor artifacts and TUF metadata to onprem offline bundle for RKE2 installs; introduces installer flag to enable arm64 vendor flow and rollback helper scripts.
commits: collect: add initial arm64 vendor artifacts + checksums
bundle: update rke2 bundle manifest + add arm64 tree and zstd compression
installer: add --enable-arm64-vendor flag + rollback helper and tests
content:
Summary: Add official arm64 vendor support to the on-prem/air-gapped offline bundle for RKE2-based installs. This PR adds arm64 binary artifacts, updates TUF metadata generation and signing, introduces a new installer flag --enable-arm64-vendor, and includes rollback helper scripts and e2e tests. Motivation: multiple enterprise customers and partners are deploying Redwood Private on ARM-based hosts (Graviton/Ampere). We need a supported, signed airgap bundle for arm64 and tooling to safely upgrade/rollback in constrained networks.

What I changed (high level):
- bundles/rke2/arm64/: new directory containing vendor binaries (rke2, cri-tools, containerd) packaged and checksummed.
- bundles/rke2/manifest.json: added arm64 entries and architecture map.
- tooling/bundle.sh: updated to collect arm64 artifacts, produce zstd-compressed archives, and emit TUF metadata for multi-arch bundles.
- tooling/tuf/: scripts to generate and sign TUF metadata; added rotation test helper for offline signing.
- installer/flags.go: new installer flag --enable-arm64-vendor and small behavior branch to prefer vendor/arm64 subdir when enabled.
- scripts/rollback-helper.sh: small utility to stage previous bundle and restore KV and manifests (used by upgrade tests).
- docs/onprem/airgap-arm64.md: usage and troubleshooting for arm64 bundles.
- test/e2e/airgap-arm64.sh: e2e that runs bundle install in an airgapped VM (QEMU) and verifies node join + simple inference smoke test.

Checklist:
- [x] Collect arm64 binaries and generate checksums.
- [x] Integrate arm64 into bundle manifest and generation script.
- [x] Add TUF metadata generation for multi-arch bundles.
- [x] Add installer flag and runtime behavior to use vendor/arm64.
- [x] Add rollback helper and e2e test that exercises upgrade+rollback.
- [x] Run CI and fix lint/test issues.

Commits: (high level)
- "collect: add initial arm64 vendor artifacts + checksums" - adds collected binaries and checksum manifests.
- "bundle: update rke2 bundle manifest + add arm64 tree and zstd compression" - bundle generation changes, adds .zst compression for size reduction.
- "installer: add --enable-arm64-vendor flag + rollback helper and tests" - installer runtime changes and tests.

Files changed (high level snippets):
- tooling/bundle.sh (+95 -28): conditional logic for ARCHS=(amd64 arm64); zstd packaging step; new tuf metadata invocation.
- bundles/rke2/manifest.json (+34 -6): new "architectures": {"arm64": {...}} entries.
- bundles/rke2/arm64/* (+binary files added): rke2-arm64.tar.zst, containerd-arm64.tar.zst, checksums.txt.
- installer/flags.go (+18 -2): Add --enable-arm64-vendor flag and runtime selection.
- scripts/rollback-helper.sh (+120 -0): added helper to stage and restore bundles during rollback tests.
- docs/onprem/airgap-arm64.md (+220 -0): doc for operators.

Review conversation highlights: 
- Marcos Silva: "Size for full arm64 bundle looks large (~1.6GB). Can we zstd it and provide incremental bundles to reduce transfer?"
  - Author reply: "Added zstd compression and an incremental manifest mode in tooling/bundle.sh; documented incremental approach in docs."
- Evelyn Park: "TUF metadata expiry and key rotation — do we have automated tests to ensure offline signing key rotation works?"
  - Author reply: "Added a small rotation test in tooling/tuf/test_rotate.sh and included instructions for offline key import in docs."
- Samir Patel: "Nit: prefer to use consistent variable naming in bundle.sh and add shellcheck directives."
  - Author reply: "Fixed variable names and addressed shellcheck issues. CI SRC check initially failed but was fixed in second commit."

CI and checks: 
- CI pipeline (linux-lint, shellcheck, unit, e2e-airgap): initial run: shellcheck failed (scripts/bundle.sh), e2e-airgap flaky failure on QEMU image provisioning. After fixes and a re-run: all checks passed. Final ci_status: pass.

Testing and validation: 
- Local manual validation on arm64 QEMU and AWS Graviton instance.
- Added e2e script that runs in GitHub Actions runner using QEMU and validates installer smoke tests in an isolated network.
- Verified TUF metadata with offline signing and verified key rotation script.

Backwards compatibility and migration: 
- Default behavior unchanged unless --enable-arm64-vendor is passed. Existing amd64-only customers unaffected. Multi-arch bundles are additive.
- Documented small operator step to opt-in and verify content signatures before installation.

Risk and mitigation: 
- Large bundle sizes: mitigated with zstd compression and documentation for incremental updates.
- TUF key misuse: added rotation test and a short admin guide to performing offline signing steps.

Merge: After addressing reviewer nits and re-running CI, this PR was approved by Marcos and Samir and merged by Evelyn Park using squash merge.

Related: Linear ENG-4123 (arm64 airgap bundles), ENG-4201 (rollback tooling). Support ticket SUP-2218 reported customer need for arm64 RKE2 bundles.
